**v1.9.1: the speedhack's error at bot start is fixed - and with `reboost` on, a blade's copies stay in hand for the hit that frees them again.**
- **The speedhack's start error is fixed.** With "Walk faster with Cheat Engine's speedhack" on, every version since v1.1.0 showed "Error: This local variable has not been assigned a value ... ceDir" when the bot started (or when you switched the speedhack on in Settings), and Cheat Engine wasn't started. A variable named like the function that finds Cheat Engine hid that function (AutoHotkey doesn't tell the two apart), and the line that starts Cheat Engine had the same mistake. Both are fixed, and a new test looks for that mistake in every one of the bot's files: it finds no other. The bot now finds Cheat Engine and starts it - debug.log "Speedhack: on - Cheat Engine started (its window minimized once it shows)".
- **Cheat Engine's window goes down to the taskbar.** "Cheat Engine.exe" only starts the build that suits your PC, at full size, so starting it minimized never reached Cheat Engine's own window (nobody saw it: the error above came first). The bot now minimizes that window as soon as it shows, the way its own minimize button does, and the window you had gets the focus back. Cheat Engine's message boxes are left for you to read.
- **With two Wizard101 windows open, Cheat Engine stays on the first.** Before, a second Wizard101 started (another account) made Cheat Engine's script move over to it within 2 s. The first was left at the walking speed, where the bot's 1x key no longer reached it, and the bot's keys sped up the second instead. After a game restart it still moves to the new one. When Cheat Engine starts with two already open, it still takes the newest. This change is in the script inside Cheat Engine: after updating, run Setup.exe once - "Cheat Engine speedhack" is ticked already (its script is older) - and press Install (Windows asks for admin).
- **Reboost - what was wrong.** With "Boost again after each hit" (`reboost`) on, a hit lets the blades it fits go again. But once a blade had gone both plain and sharpened (with a Sharpened Blade on it), the bot's DiscardSpare threw that blade's other copies away: its both-casts rule didn't look at `reboost`. The simulator has played it that way since v1.9.0, and v1.9.0's notes measured what it cost.
- **What changes in the game.** Only with `reboost` on, as a Hitter (or with the party off), not with Alt+2's pick: those copies now stay in your hand and go again after the next hit the blade fits. debug.log says so once a battle a blade: "storm/blade: its plain and sharpened casts both went - its copies kept in hand: with reboost on, the next hit it fits lets it go again (said once a battle)". A spare Sharpen is still thrown once no blade in hand can take one: it helps (v1.9.0 measured 52.9% for the first deck below against the mobs with both rules off, against 57.0% with only the both-casts rule off, as v1.9.1 plays). Unchanged: `reboost` off (the default); a party's Blader or Healer with the party on, whatever round it plays; Alt+2's pick (left as it was: its blades mostly go on another wizard's plate, whose casts your hit doesn't free); traps (this rule never threw them); `discardspent` (it never runs with `reboost` on).
- **The simulator plays it** (the boss deck pick, the planner, the zone deck) when the AutoFarmer says it keeps them: this AutoFarmer sends one more value with its settings, `reboostkeep:1`, or 0 as a Blader or Healer with the party on and with Alt+2's pick, where the bot still throws them - so those results stay as they were.
- **Measured on the same dice** (2000 battles a cell, each battle on the same seed in v1.9.0 and v1.9.1): a Storm wizard with 3000 health and 60% damage against a 6000-health boss or 3 mobs of 1500 health (2-pip hits of 150-200 and 100-150 that always land), `reboost` on. % won v1.9.0 -> v1.9.1; in brackets, the battles only v1.9.1 won / only v1.9.0 won:
  - 8 Storm Lord + 3 Stormblade + 3 Sharpened Blade: the boss 93.7% -> 94.6% (+58 / -39); 3 mobs 44.5% -> 57.0% (+333 / -84). v1.8.1's simulator won 64.3% against the mobs: it threw the Sharpens away at once. The rest of that gap is the Sharpen played as the bot plays it - held for a blade, and the sharpened cast one more boosting round before a hit.
  - 8 Storm Lord + 6 Stormblade + 6 Storm Trap + 2 Sharpened Blade + 2 Potent Trap: the boss 97.2% -> 97.1% (+2 / -4); 3 mobs 75.3% -> 75.3% (+115 / -115).
  - 4 Storm Lord + 4 Tempest + 3 Stormblade + 3 Storm Trap + 2 Feint + 2 Sharpened Blade + 2 Potent Trap: the boss 96.8% -> 97.2% (+13 / -5); 3 mobs 89.9% -> 90.2% (+43 / -36).
  - 8 Storm Lord + 1 Stormblade + 1 Sharpened Blade, and 10 Thunder Snake + 6 Storm Lord + 4 Sharpened Blade (no blade): the same battles won - no second copy to keep.
  - With `reboost` off (`discardspent` on or off), and with `reboost` on but the value not sent (an older AutoFarmer): every cell the same, battle for battle.
- **The simulator plays everything else exactly as before**, against v1.9.0: 90 random decks without Sharpen or Potent (1890 simulate, 450 planner, 90 team plan and 90 deck pick comparisons, sent the value and not) and 45 random decks with Sharpen, 20 of them with Potent too (1755 simulate, 184 planner as Hitter, Blader and Healer, 23 team plan and 45 deck pick comparisons wherever the bot doesn't change: the value not sent, `reboost` off, or a support), 0 differing.
- **Mixed versions are fine.** An older AutoFarmer with this helper sends no `reboostkeep`: its simulator throws the copies as that bot does, so its results are v1.9.0's. This AutoFarmer with an older helper: the helper ignores the value and plays as before; the zone deck is worked out once more after updating.
- **Not tried in the game yet.** The bot's changes were only read, not run against the game (no AutoHotkey or Cheat Engine where they were made): AutoFarmer\LIVE_CHECKS.txt steps 2.10 (reboost), 5.3 and 5.5 (the speedhack) say what to look for and what to send.
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install, including ones set up from the v0.7.0 or v0.7.1 zips. Your settings, learned cards and routes are kept. A copy run from the code: git pull.
